title: Video follow-up, knee, return to running

transcript.speaker: clinician
transcript.text: Hi Sofia, I can see you on video. Tell me about the knee.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: The front of my knee aches after runs. It's about 3 out of 10 after a 5K, and zero when I'm resting.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Two. I cut my distance in half.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: A little after the second run. It was gone by morning.

transcript.speaker: clinician
transcript.text: Are you doing the single-leg squat progression?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Three sets of eight on the right leg, a little harder on the left.

transcript.speaker: clinician
transcript.text: Has the knee been waking you up at night?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: No, it doesn't wake me up.

transcript.speaker: clinician
transcript.text: Plan: keep runs under three miles for two weeks. If the knee stays pain-free at rest, we'll add run-walk intervals. I'd like to see you in person in three weeks for a strength test.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Okay, I'll stay under three miles.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: My goal is to run the half marathon in March.

transcript.speaker: clinician
transcript.text: Let's be realistic about March, and we'll check progress at the in-person visit.

expectedFacts.statement: Front of knee aches after runs, 3 out of 10 after a 5K
Swelling after second run, gone by morning
Three sets of eight single-leg squats
Knee does not wake the patient at night
Keep runs under three miles for two weeks
In-person visit in three weeks for a strength test
Goal: run the half marathon in March
